source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten references. ECMAScript Promise states, jobs, resolution, aggregation, and empty-race behavior were checked against ECMA-262 and WHATWG; interoperability against Promises/A+; Java continuation and cancellation behavior against Java 25 CompletionStage and CompletableFuture; C++ ownership against the current working draft; Rust polling and wake semantics against official Rust documentation; Python executor futures against Python 3 documentation; and structured ownership status against JEP 525. Cross-runtime contrasts remain scoped to cited APIs.

evidence: Definitions and Notation defines sigma states, admitted A, running R, cleanup K, queue Q_c, and service S_c before use.
Pending, fulfilled, rejected, and optional cancellation states remain distinct from operation, observer, and task ownership.
notation_and_syntax.notes: State, bound, continuation-time, and aggregate notation was checked for consistent domains and comparisons.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/CONPAR-033/report.json records source value 21, mapped value 42, one winning and one rejected settlement, and zero queued jobs.
Manual FIFO replay gives early:21, late:21, mapped:42 because the mapped observer is enqueued only when the second source reaction runs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The first expected trace was corrected after execution exposed the nested enqueue order; the final exact output matches the queue model.

evidence: Single assignment permits exactly one transition from PENDING to one tagged terminal state.
Fail-fast settlement was independently checked not to imply forall i settled(F_i); bounded ownership separately requires |A|<=q and |R|<=k.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The implications distinguish public aggregate outcome from lifecycle termination and admission from active execution.

evidence: Reviewed early and late observers, duplicate and self-settlement, empty and duplicate aggregate inputs, eager and lazy work, absent handlers, nested futures, and unhandled branches.

Reviewed timeout/completion races, cancellation acknowledgement, late resources, executor starvation, dropped polling futures, retained context, shutdown, remote effects, and safety-critical transfer.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary review covers temporal, cardinality, scheduling, capacity, ownership, memory-publication, cancellation, remote, and deployment risks.

evidence: Only the first settlement publishes the tagged payload; every registered reaction is queued exactly once by the teaching model.
Every started loser remains owned after race, timeout, or fail-fast aggregate settlement until cancellation and cleanup are observed.
invariant_checking.notes: Invariants were checked across success, failure, timeout, duplicate settlement, cancellation, aggregation, and shutdown paths.

evidence: The single-assignment argument maps every completion attempt to one PENDING test and one irreversible winning transition.
The aggregate counterexample uses a public early rejection while sibling inputs remain nonterminal, disproving any inferred join property.
proof_review.notes: Arguments are conditional on declared scheduler and API semantics and do not assert universal cancellation or memory behavior.

evidence: ECMAScript, Java, C++, and Rust claims are named as runtime-specific rather than portable laws.
Executable limitations explicitly exclude rejection, assimilation, threads, polling, cancellation, deadlines, aggregation, backpressure, and cleanup.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Specification facts, portable design invariants, teaching-model evidence, and external-review requirements remain distinct.

evidence: python3 tools/verify_snippets.py CONPAR-033 passed with exact stdout, empty stderr, and Python toolchain evidence.
Queue latency, real executor ordering, cancellation timing, I/O interruption, remote completion, and physical safety are identified as empirical.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The deterministic run validates only the stipulated single-thread FIFO model and proves no runtime or device behavior.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed observation versus completion authority versus task execution; state and publication; scheduling; mapping, flattening, assimilation; eager/lazy work; combinators; failure ownership; blocking; cancellation; deadlines; polling/wakers; sharing; context; and API selection.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed least-authority interfaces, explicit executors, bounded producer admission, all/race loser ownership, timeout arbitration, late-resource disposal, starvation avoidance, error-cause preservation, context propagation, finite shutdown, and evidence-visible detached supervision.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet states the portable model and caveats; exposition progresses from authority through composition and lifecycle; ten examples cover distinct transfer cases; five exercises progress from definitions to capacity, races, and safety-critical review with matching answers.

limitations: Internal authoring and verification evidence only; no external language-runtime, academic, practitioner, distributed-systems, security, medical, railway, regulatory, or functional-safety review is claimed. The executable model does not establish real scheduling, memory publication, cancellation, cleanup, remote, or deployment correctness.
